candidates.rationale: Weakest component is the numerator anchor. It measures adjusted $close against a raw high/low range, so the ratio carries each name's dividend adjustment factor, which is built from future dividends; the anchor is also a single 21d extreme low that one panic print pins for a month, matching the decay from +0.025 (2000-02) to +0.001 (2013). Putting every leg on the raw OHLC scale and centering on the mean low removes the leak and the stale extreme. Denominator and windows untouched.

The price leg divides a distance by a price level, so it is really range-over-price, a volatility ratio that drifts with each name's price level; that is where the 2003 and 2012 sign flips (stability 0.86, ICIR 0.081) come from. Dividing by the 21d dispersion of the same raw series makes the leg a unit-free position comparable across names and regimes. Fundamental leg untouched.

The 189d leg is the binding weakness: coverage is 0.904, one bad quarter from the 0.90 gate, because a nine-month window drops recent index entrants, and it divides adjusted $close by a raw high so the rank picks up the forward-looking adjustment factor. A same-scale raw $open over a 21d high keeps the idea, restores coverage, and complies with the 21-bar cap; the vol leg is left alone so only one component moves.

Bare $volume is a share-count level, so most of its cross-sectional variation is permanent float and size, not forecast: IC half-life exceeds 63 days yet it still pays 0.153 one-way turnover, and it sits at 0.717 against TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21). Ranking each name's volume inside its own 21d history strips the static float exposure and leaves abnormal activity, adding exactly one operator to the bare field.

candidates.changed_node: root: RANK($roa) grafted as the left operand of a difference against RANK($accrual_gap)
candidates.rationale: The weakness is that a level of profitability carries no earnings-quality control, so it flips in junk rallies (2003 -0.0045, 2006 -0.0026) and sits at 0.723 against the archive's quality composite. Following the island rule, RANK($roa) is grafted whole as one operand rather than dismantled, and paired with a second cross-sectionally ranked fundamental; the accrual leg enters with a minus, matching the negative fitted sign the archive already gives $accrual_gap.

The range leg is a single-day print: it burns 0.291 one-way turnover on a factor whose IC half-life is 40 days, so it churns daily for information that moves monthly, and its very short horizon is what holds |rho| at 0.765 against the 2/5-bar accrual-range archive member. Averaging the raw range over 21 bars matches the leg to the factor's own decay; the normalizer stays a raw OHLC field and the accrual leg is untouched.

The 2-bar windows are the weak component: IC half-life 3.4 days against 0.656 one-way turnover, 0.022 of fitness burned, and only 0.71 of years positive, a two-day overlap measure asked to forecast well past its life. At 21 bars the identical structure becomes a trend-efficiency ratio, the monthly range over the sum of daily ranges, turning over roughly a tenth as often. Fields and structure unchanged.

The aggregated field is the weakness: a 21d mean of dollar volume is a size proxy, which is why half-life exceeds 63 days, |rho| is 0.717 against raw $volume, and the IC flips whenever size leadership does (2005, 2007). The dollar-volume family is exhausted on this island, so the same single-operator shape is kept and pointed at $return, giving a 21d mean return outside that family with full coverage and no added complexity charge.

The 10-day EMA reference sets the signal's horizon and it is too fast: IC half-life 3.1 days on 0.292 turnover, with the weekly component going the wrong way in 2010, 2011 and 2012 (stability 0.71). Measuring displacement against a 21-day EMA aligns the numerator with the 21-day denominator and with a monthly reversal horizon, slowing the signal and cutting churn. Everything else is unchanged, and the expression stays entirely on the adjusted $close scale.

The volume multiplier is the weakest part: a single-day spike ratio drives 0.638 one-way turnover (0.016 of fitness) on a factor with a 48-day half-life, and its 42-bar base window sits in the range that has only ever appeared in rejects. Smoothing it to a 5-over-21 relative-activity ratio keeps the intraday leg exactly as is, cuts the churn, and brings every window under the 21-bar cap.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Read the diagnostics: a factor whose IC is positive in most years and negative in two has a regime problem, one with high turnover is paying costs it does not earn back, and one whose IC half-life is short is being asked to predict too far ahead. Change the component responsible for the specific weakness you name.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Stop proposing new normalizations of $dollar_volume alone. Every such aggregate this round clustered at |t| 0.72-0.82 on the cheap window: TS_SUM($return*$dollar_volume), TS_MAX/TS_SUM, TS_COV with $return, SIGN counts, and TS_RANK crossed with $leverage all failed, and the two that passed reached only 0.715 and 0.824 fitness. That family is exhausted on this island.
  2. Try the bare field or a single-operator version before deep nesting. Raw $volume scored 3.839 while every multi-operator $dollar_volume transform scored under 0.9; the extra structure paid the complexity charge without earning it back.
  3. Spend the round in the mixed niche (fundamental rank against an intraday-range term). It produced the two best results by a wide margin: RANK($roa) versus a 21d low/high position at 4.355, and CS_RANK($accrual_gap) with a range/open ratio at 2.884. The price_volume/high niche is saturated near the gate.
  4. Cross-sectionally normalize both legs before combining them. RANK($roa) minus a ranked price term scored 4.355; the same fundamental multiplied by a raw unbounded price ratio scored 0.20 on the cheap screen. Never combine a rank with an unnormalized signed price quantity.
  5. Keep lookbacks at 21 bars or fewer. Accepted expressions used only 2 and 21 bar windows; 42, 63, 126, and 189 bar lookbacks appeared exclusively in rejected proposals.
  6. Drop conditional regime splits. The single IF_ELSE proposal, switching between short-horizon reversal and momentum on high-low versus its 21d mean, had the worst cheap screen of the round at 0.48.
  7. RANK($roa) is too small to serve as a crossover parent. Both children built around it kept almost none of it while adding long-window volatility and price-extreme terms. Graft it whole as one operand of a larger donor expression, or cross from a bigger parent subtree instead.
  8. Normalize intraday-range terms by a raw OHLC field, as the accepted ones do with $open and ($high - $low). Do not divide OHLC quantities by $close: $close is adjusted while OHLC is raw, so mixing the scales is a units error that imports future dividend information.
